cohort: Fifteen caregiver-child dyads (caregivers predominantly mothers, Black, and lower-socioeconomic status; children predominantly female and Black, with a mean age of 3.0 years) participating in an urban primary care setting.
finding: The brief, early childhood behavioral sleep intervention, Sleep Well!, was feasible to implement in urban primary care for families from primarily lower-socioeconomic status and/or racially minoritized backgrounds, demonstrating strong acceptability, cultural humility, and positive initial improvements in child sleep metrics.
